Make pickling liquid, approximately 3:2:1 your choice of vinegar:sugar:water plus some salt. If you have aromatics around throw them in there too but strain them out at the end. You can also buy pickling spice that has such aromatics (juniper, allspice, clove, bay leaf, mustard seed, chili flake, etc) already blended. Anyhow make this liquid and bring it to a boil and if it tastes too acidic or too sweet or not acidic enough or not sweet enough you can easily correct this because you're not an idiot. You make enough pickling liquid to cover your beets, which you have peeled and cut up into bite sized pieces while the liquid is heating up and the sugar and salt crystals are dissolving into a solution. Put the beets in the hot liquid or pour the hot liquid over the beets, it doesn't matter. Get them to al dente, don't cook them to mush. remember to account for carryover cooking and taste constantly. Then cool them down in your fridge.
